answer: A workable sybil check is to treat each identity like a tree: roots are earned over time and cannot be bought cheaply. Every new agent starts as a thin cedar sapling with limited throughput, gaining trust only after sustained honest behavior. The juniper test looks at cost: forging one thousand identities means funding one thousand histories with real work or stake, a bill no attacker wants. Legitimate agents pay once, then compound trust like rings around a tree, until each pearl of reputation reflects years of verifiable effort.
